verses.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἤρξατο διδάσκειν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ συνάγεται πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλος πλεῖστος ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἦσαν
verses.transliteration: Kai palin ērxato didaskein para tēn thalassan kai synagetai pros auton ochlos pleistos hōste auton eis ploion embanta kathēsthai en tē thalassē kai pas ho ochlos pros tēn thalassan epi tēs gēs ēsan
verses.literal: Once again Jesus began to teach beside the sea and such a large crowd gathered around Him that He got into . . . a boat and sat in it while all the people crowded . . . . . . . . . along the shore
verses.literalPt: De novo, começou Jesus a ensinar à beira do mar. Reuniu-se a ele uma grande multidão, de maneira que entrou numa barca e sentou-se dentro dela no mar; e todo o povo achava-se na praia.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς πολλά καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai edidasken autous en parabolais polla kai elegen autois en tē didachē autou
verses.literal: And He taught them many things in parables and in His teaching He said
verses.literalPt: Ele lhes ensinava muitas coisas por parábolas, dizendo, no correr do seu ensino:

verses.original: Ἀκούετε ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων σπεῖραι
verses.transliteration: Akouete idou exēlthen ho speirōn speirai
verses.literal: Listen . . . A farmer went out to sow his seed
verses.literalPt: Ouvi: O semeador saiu a semear;

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ σπείρειν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν καὶ ἦλθεν τὰ πετεινὰ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτό
verses.transliteration: kai egeneto en tō speirein ho men epesen para tēn hodon kai ēlthen ta peteina kai katephagen auto
verses.literal: And as he was sowing some seed fell along the path and the birds came and devoured it
verses.literalPt: quando semeava, uma parte da semente caiu à beira do caminho, e vieram as aves e comeram-na.

verses.original: Καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸ πετρῶδες ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν καὶ εὐθὺς ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς
verses.transliteration: Kai allo epesen epi to petrōdes hopou ouk eichen gēn pollēn kai euthys exaneteilen dia to mē echein bathos gēs
verses.literal: Some fell on rocky ground where it did not have much soil It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow . . . . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: Outra parte caiu nos lugares pedregosos, onde não havia muita terra; logo nasceu, porque a terra não era profunda.

verses.original: καὶ ὅτε ἀνέτειλεν ὁ ἥλιος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη
verses.transliteration: kai hote aneteilen ho hēlios ekaumatisthē kai dia to mē echein rhizan exēranthē
verses.literal: But when the sun rose the seedlings were scorched and they withered because they had no root
verses.literalPt: E, tendo saído o sol, queimou-se; e, porque não tinha raiz, secou-se.

verses.original: Καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ συνέπνιξαν αὐτό καὶ καρπὸν οὐκ ἔδωκεν
verses.transliteration: Kai allo epesen eis tas akanthas kai anebēsan hai akanthai kai synepnixan auto kai karpon ouk edōken
verses.literal: Other seed fell among thorns - which grew up and choked the seedlings and they yielded no crop
verses.literalPt: Outra caiu entre os espinhos; e os espinhos cresceram e sufocaram-na, e não deu fruto algum.

verses.original: Καὶ ἄλλα ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν καλήν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπὸν ἀναβαίνοντα καὶ αὐξανόμενα καὶ ἔφερεν ἓν τριάκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑκατόν
verses.transliteration: Kai alla epesen eis tēn gēn tēn kalēn kai edidou karpon anabainonta kai auxanomena kai epheren hen triakonta kai hen hexēkonta kai hen hekaton
verses.literal: Still other seed fell on - good soil where it sprouted grew up and produced a crop one bearing thirtyfold another sixtyfold and another a hundredfold
verses.literalPt: Mas outras caíram na boa terra e, brotando e crescendo, davam fruto; um grão produzia trinta; outro, sessenta; e outro, cem.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν Ὃς ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen Hos echei ōta akouein akouetō
verses.literal: Then Jesus said He who has ears to hear let him hear
verses.literalPt: Disse: Quem tem ouvidos para ouvir, ouça.

verses.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο κατὰ μόνας ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν σὺν τοῖς δώδεκα τὰς παραβολάς
verses.transliteration: Kai hote egeneto kata monas ērōtōn auton hoi peri auton syn tois dōdeka tas parabolas
verses.literal: As soon as . . . Jesus was alone with the Twelve and those around Him they asked Him about the parable
verses.literalPt: Quando se achou só, os que estavam ao redor dele com os doze pediam a explicação das parábolas.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμῖν τὸ μυστήριον δέδοται τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐκείνοις δὲ τοῖς ἔξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὰ πάντα γίνεται
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autois Hymin to mystērion dedotai tēs basileias tou Theou ekeinois de tois exō en parabolais ta panta ginetai
verses.literal: He replied The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you but to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables
verses.literalPt: Ele lhes disse: A vós vos é dado o mistério do reino de Deus; mas aos de fora tudo se lhes propõe em parábolas,

verses.original: ἵνα Βλέποντες βλέπωσιν καὶ μὴ ἴδωσιν Καὶ ἀκούοντες ἀκούωσιν καὶ μὴ συνιῶσιν Μή‿ ποτε ἐπιστρέψωσιν Καὶ ἀφεθῇ αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: hina Blepontes blepōsin kai mē idōsin Kai akouontes akouōsin kai mē syniōsin Mē pote epistrepsōsin Kai aphethē autois
verses.literal: so that they may be ever seeing but never perceiving and ever hearing but never understanding otherwise . . . they might turn and be forgiven . . .
verses.literalPt: para que, vendo, vejam, e não percebam; e, ouvindo, ouçam e não entendam, para que não suceda que se convertam e sejam perdoados.

verses.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην καὶ πῶς πάσας τὰς παραβολὰς γνώσεσθε
verses.transliteration: Kai legei autois Ouk oidate tēn parabolēn tautēn kai pōs pasas tas parabolas gnōsesthe
verses.literal: Then Jesus said to them Do you not understand this parable Then how will you understand any of the parables
verses.literalPt: Perguntou-lhes: Não percebeis esta parábola e como entendereis todas as parábolas?

verses.original: Ὁ σπείρων τὸν λόγον σπείρει
verses.transliteration: Ho speirōn ton logon speirei
verses.literal: The farmer sows the word
verses.literalPt: O semeador semeia a palavra.

verses.original: οὗτοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ὅπου σπείρεται ὁ λόγος καὶ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν εὐθὺς ἔρχεται ὁ Σατανᾶς καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον τὸν ἐσπαρμένον εἰς αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: houtoi de eisin hoi para tēn hodon hopou speiretai ho logos kai hotan akousōsin euthys erchetai ho Satanas kai airei ton logon ton esparmenon eis autous
verses.literal: Some are like the seeds along the path where the word is sown As soon as . . . they hear it Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them
verses.literalPt: Os que se acham pelo caminho, onde a palavra é semeada são aqueles, de quem, depois de a terem ouvido, vindo logo Satanás, tira a palavra que neles tem sido semeada.

verses.original: Καὶ οὗτοί εἰσιν ὁμοίως οἱ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπειρόμενοι οἳ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνουσιν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Kai houtoi eisin homoiōs hoi epi ta petrōdē speiromenoi hoi hotan akousōsin ton logon euthys meta charas lambanousin auton
verses.literal: Some are like the seeds sown on rocky ground They hear the word and at once receive it with joy
verses.literalPt: Igualmente, os semeados nos lugares pedregosos são aqueles que, ouvindo a palavra, imediatamente, a recebem com alegria;

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιροί εἰσιν εἶτα γενομένης θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζονται
verses.transliteration: kai ouk echousin rhizan en heautois alla proskairoi eisin eita genomenēs thlipseōs ē diōgmou dia ton logon euthys skandalizontai
verses.literal: But they themselves have . . . . . . no root and they remain for only a season When trouble or persecution comes because of the word they quickly fall away
verses.literalPt: eles não têm em si raiz, mas duram pouco tempo; depois, sobrevindo tribulação ou perseguição por causa da palavra, logo se escandalizam.

verses.original: Καὶ ἄλλοι εἰσὶν οἱ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπειρόμενοι οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον ἀκούσαντες
verses.transliteration: Kai alloi eisin hoi eis tas akanthas speiromenoi houtoi eisin hoi ton logon akousantes
verses.literal: Others . . . are like the seeds sown among the thorns They . . . . . . hear the word
verses.literalPt: Os outros, os semeados entre os espinhos, são os que ouvem a palavra,

verses.original: καὶ αἱ μέριμναι τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου καὶ αἱ περὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ἐπιθυμίαι εἰσπορευόμεναι συμπνίγουσιν τὸν λόγον καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται
verses.transliteration: kai hai merimnai tou aiōnos kai hē apatē tou ploutou kai hai peri ta loipa epithymiai eisporeuomenai sympnigousin ton logon kai akarpos ginetai
verses.literal: but the worries of this life the deceitfulness of wealth and the desire for other things come in and choke the word and it becomes unfruitful
verses.literalPt: e os cuidados do mundo, a sedução das riquezas e a cobiça de outras coisas, entrando, abafam a palavra, e ela fica infrutífera.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐκεῖνοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν σπαρέντες οἵτινες ἀκούουσιν τὸν λόγον καὶ παραδέχονται καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ἓν τριάκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑκατόν
verses.transliteration: Kai ekeinoi eisin hoi epi tēn gēn tēn kalēn sparentes hoitines akouousin ton logon kai paradechontai kai karpophorousin hen triakonta kai hen hexēkonta kai hen hekaton
verses.literal: Still others are like the seeds sown on - good soil They hear the word receive it and produce a crop thirtyfold - sixtyfold or a hundredfold
verses.literalPt: Os semeados na boa terra são os que ouvem a palavra, e a recebem, e produzem fruto, a trinta, a sessenta e a cem por um.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Μήτι ἔρχεται ὁ λύχνος ἵνα ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον τεθῇ ἢ ὑπὸ τὴν κλίνην οὐχ ἵνα ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν τεθῇ
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autois hoti Mēti erchetai ho lychnos hina hypo ton modion tethē ē hypo tēn klinēn ouch hina epi tēn lychnian tethē
verses.literal: Jesus also said to them Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed Doesn’t he set it on a stand
verses.literalPt: Continuou: Porventura, vem a candeia para se pôr debaixo do módio ou debaixo da cama? Não é, antes, para se colocar no velador?

verses.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν τι κρυπτὸν ἐὰν μὴ ἵνα φανερωθῇ οὐδὲ ἐγένετο ἀπόκρυφον ἀλλ’ ἵνα ἔλθῃ εἰς φανερόν
verses.transliteration: ou gar estin ti krypton ean mē hina phanerōthē oude egeneto apokryphon all’ hina elthē eis phaneron
verses.literal: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed and nothing concealed that will not be brought to light
verses.literalPt: Pois nada está oculto, senão para ser manifesto; e nada foi escondido, senão para ser divulgado.

verses.original: Εἴ τις ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω
verses.transliteration: Ei tis echei ōta akouein akouetō
verses.literal: If anyone has ears to hear let him hear
verses.literalPt: Se alguém tem ouvidos para ouvir, ouça.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Βλέπετε τί ἀκούετε ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν καὶ προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autois Blepete ti akouete en hō metrō metreite metrēthēsetai hymin kai prostethēsetai hymin
verses.literal: He went on to say Pay attention to what you hear With the measure you use it will be measured to you and even more will be added to you
verses.literalPt: Também lhes disse: Atendei ao que ouvis. A medida de que usais, desta usarão convosco; e ainda se vos acrescentará.

verses.original: ὃς γὰρ ἔχει δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ ὃς οὐκ ἔχει καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: hos gar echei dothēsetai autō kai hos ouk echei kai ho echei arthēsetai ap’ autou
verses.literal: For whoever has will be given more But whoever does not have even what he has will be taken away from him
verses.literalPt: Pois ao que tem ser-lhe-á dado; e ao que não tem, até aquilo que tem, ser-lhe-á tirado.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν Οὕτως ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ ὡς ἄνθρωπος βάλῃ τὸν σπόρον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen Houtōs estin hē basileia tou Theou hōs anthrōpos balē ton sporon epi tēs gēs
verses.literal: Jesus also said The kingdom of God is like . . . a man who scatters seed on the ground
verses.literalPt: Disse mais: O reino de Deus é como se um homem lançasse a semente na terra

verses.original: καὶ καθεύδῃ καὶ ἐγείρηται νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ ὁ σπόρος βλαστᾷ καὶ μηκύνηται ὡς οὐκ οἶδεν αὐτός
verses.transliteration: kai katheudē kai egeirētai nykta kai hēmeran kai ho sporos blasta kai mēkynētai hōs ouk oiden autos
verses.literal: Night and day he sleeps and wakes and the seed sprouts and grows though he knows not how
verses.literalPt: e, dormindo ou acordado de noite e de dia, a semente germinasse e crescesse, sem ele saber como.

verses.original: αὐτομάτη ἡ γῆ καρποφορεῖ πρῶτον χόρτον εἶτα στάχυν εἶτα πλήρης σῖτον ἐν τῷ στάχυϊ
verses.transliteration: automatē hē gē karpophorei prōton chorton eita stachyn eita plērēs siton en tō stachui
verses.literal: All by itself the earth produces a crop first the stalk then the head then grain that ripens within . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: A terra por si mesma produz fruto: primeiro, a erva, depois, a espiga e, por último, o grão grado na espiga.

verses.original: ὅταν δὲ παραδοῖ ὁ καρπός εὐθὺς ἀποστέλλει τὸ δρέπανον ὅτι παρέστηκεν ὁ θερισμός
verses.transliteration: hotan de paradoi ho karpos euthys apostellei to drepanon hoti parestēken ho therismos
verses.literal: And as soon as . . . the grain is ripe he swings the sickle because the harvest has come
verses.literalPt: Depois de o fruto amadurecer, logo lhe mete a foice, porque é chegada a ceifa.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν Πῶς ὁμοιώσωμεν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἢ ἐν τίνι αὐτὴν παραβολῇ θῶμεν
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen Pōs homoiōsōmen tēn basileian tou Theou ē en tini autēn parabolē thōmen
verses.literal: Then He asked To what can we compare the kingdom of God With what parable shall we present it
verses.literalPt: Ainda disse: A que assemelharemos o reino de Deus ou com que parábola o representaremos?

verses.original: ὡς κόκκῳ σινάπεως ὃς ὅταν σπαρῇ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς μικρότερον ὂν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
verses.transliteration: hōs kokkō sinapeōs hos hotan sparē epi tēs gēs mikroteron on pantōn tōn spermatōn tōn epi tēs gēs
verses.literal: It is like a mustard seed . . . which is the smallest of all seeds sown . . . . . . . . . upon the earth
verses.literalPt: É como um grão de mostarda, que, quando semeado na terra, embora seja menor que todas as sementes que há na terra,

verses.original: καὶ ὅταν σπαρῇ ἀναβαίνει καὶ γίνεται μεῖζον πάντων τῶν λαχάνων καὶ ποιεῖ κλάδους μεγάλους ὥστε δύνασθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σκιὰν αὐτοῦ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνοῦν
verses.transliteration: kai hotan sparē anabainei kai ginetai meizon pantōn tōn lachanōn kai poiei kladous megalous hōste dynasthai hypo tēn skian autou ta peteina tou ouranou kataskēnoun
verses.literal: But after it is planted it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches so that the birds of the air nest in its shade
verses.literalPt: contudo, depois de semeado, cresce e se torna a maior de todas as hortaliças e deita grandes ramos, de tal modo que as aves do céu podem pousar à sua sombra.

verses.original: Καὶ τοιαύταις παραβολαῖς πολλαῖς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον καθὼς ἠδύναντο ἀκούειν
verses.transliteration: Kai toiautais parabolais pollais elalei autois ton logon kathōs ēdynanto akouein
verses.literal: With many such parables Jesus spoke the word to them to the extent that they could understand
verses.literalPt: Com muitas parábolas semelhantes dirigia-lhes a palavra, conforme podiam compreendê-la;

verses.original: χωρὶς δὲ παραβολῆς οὐκ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς κατ’ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς ἰδίοις μαθηταῖς ἐπέλυεν πάντα
verses.transliteration: chōris de parabolēs ouk elalei autois kat’ idian de tois idiois mathētais epelyen panta
verses.literal: He did not tell them anything . . . without using a parable But privately He explained everything to His own disciples
verses.literalPt: não lhes falava sem parábolas, mas em particular explicava tudo a seus discípulos.

verses.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὀψίας γενομένης Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν
verses.transliteration: Kai legei autois en ekeinē tē hēmera opsias genomenēs Dielthōmen eis to peran
verses.literal: When that evening came He said to His disciples Let us cross to the other side
verses.literalPt: Naquele dia, à tarde, lhes disse: Passemos para o outro lado.

verses.original: καὶ ἀφέντες τὸν ὄχλον παραλαμβάνουσιν αὐτὸν ὡς ἦν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ καὶ ἄλλα πλοῖα ἦν μετ’ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai aphentes ton ochlon paralambanousin auton hōs ēn en tō ploiō kai alla ploia ēn met’ autou
verses.literal: After they had dismissed the crowd they took Jesus with them . . . since He was already in the boat And there were other boats with Him
verses.literalPt: Eles, deixando a multidão, o levaram, assim como estava, na barca; e estavam com ele outras barcas.

verses.original: Καὶ γίνεται λαῖλαψ μεγάλη ἀνέμου καὶ τὰ κύματα ἐπέβαλλεν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ὥστε ἤδη γεμίζεσθαι τὸ πλοῖον
verses.transliteration: Kai ginetai lailaps megalē anemou kai ta kymata epeballen eis to ploion hōste ēdē gemizesthai to ploion
verses.literal: Soon a violent windstorm . . . came up and the waves were breaking over the boat so that it was being swamped
verses.literalPt: Levantou-se um grande tufão de vento, e as ondas batiam na barca, de modo que ela já se enchia.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἐν τῇ πρύμνῃ ἐπὶ τὸ προσκεφάλαιον καθεύδων καὶ ἐγείρουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε οὐ μέλει σοι ὅτι ἀπολλύμεθα
verses.transliteration: kai autos ēn en tē prymnē epi to proskephalaion katheudōn kai egeirousin auton kai legousin autō Didaskale ou melei soi hoti apollymetha
verses.literal: But Jesus was in the stern sleeping on the cushion So they woke Him and said Teacher don’t You care . . . that we are perishing
verses.literalPt: Jesus estava dormindo na popa sobre o travesseiro; eles o acordaram e lhe perguntaram: Mestre, não se te dá que pereçamos?

verses.original: Καὶ διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ εἶπεν τῇ θαλάσσῃ Σιώπα πεφίμωσο καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη μεγάλη
verses.transliteration: Kai diegertheis epetimēsen tō anemō kai eipen tē thalassē Siōpa pephimōso kai ekopasen ho anemos kai egeneto galēnē megalē
verses.literal: Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea Silence He commanded Be still And the wind died down and it was perfectly calm
verses.literalPt: Ele, tendo acordado, repreendeu o vento e disse ao mar: Cala-te, emudece. Cessou o vento, e houve grande bonança.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί δειλοί ἐστε οὔπω ἔχετε πίστιν
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen autois Ti deiloi este oupō echete pistin
verses.literal: Why are you so afraid He asked Do you still have no . . . faith
verses.literalPt: Então lhes perguntou: Por que sois assim tímidos? Como é que não tendes fé?

verses.original: Καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἀλλήλους Τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ ἡ θάλασσα ὑπακούει αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Kai ephobēthēsan phobon megan kai elegon pros allēlous Tis ara houtos estin hoti kai ho anemos kai hē thalassa hypakouei autō
verses.literal: Overwhelmed with fear . . . . . . they asked . . . one another Who is this that even the wind and the sea obey Him
verses.literalPt: Eles, cheios de medo, diziam uns aos outros: Quem, porventura, é este que até o vento e o mar lhe obedecem?
